source.title: Attention as a Routing Graph: Live Circuit Extraction from a Single Forward Pass

record.tranche_reason: It tests causal importance on induction prompts using attention-edge ablation and a task-score measure, rather than measuring induction-head formation or using the original training-dynamics method.
record.gate_note: The induction-task ablations bear on causal routes used for induction. IOI results concern a different task and are not rows for these claim versions. Section 3.5 reports extraction-setting sensitivities, but those settings are used to tune the sketch and do not directly test induction-head formation or in-context learning dynamics.
record.test_reason: Induction prompts serve as a benchmark with a known circuit, used to validate the authors' attention-routing extraction method. All results compare the method's selected-edge ablation with random-edge ablation. No result measures whether induction heads exist, how they compose, when they form, or how much in-context learning they carry. The models are full transformers, not small attention-only ones. The heads overlapping the walk (L4H11, L5H5, L5H8) are labelled from prior work, not identified as induction heads here.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that a cheap single-pass attention-routing sketch carries real causal signal on induction and IOI in three small open models. They add that it is incomplete, may be inflated by attention-mass effects, and has identifiable failure modes.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts attention edges from a forward pass and tests them by edge ablation against random-edge controls; it does not test training-time emergence or induction-head composition as in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: On GPT-2 Small induction, the reported sketch result depends on using enough of the graph and the right layers: k=5 is unreliable, k≥10 is reported as fine, late layers alone fail, and early layers alone recover most of the gap. A harsh score threshold loses signal; product scoring is a little better than raw attention. Changing the prompt template or adding a few filler sentences does not eliminate the gap.

fits_no_version.finding: On induction prompts, ablating edges extracted in a single forward pass drops the target logit far more than ablating same-size random edge sets. Gaps are +4.33 (GPT-2 Small), +1.51 (GPT-2 Medium) and +2.25 (Pythia-410M). The authors note part of each gap may be an unmeasured attention-mass effect. Early layers alone recover most of the gap on GPT-2 Small.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single-forward attention-routing sketch recovers routes causally relevant to induction-task predictions in small pretrained LMs, beyond same-size random edges.

record.problems: The authors note that the selected edges remove more attention mass than the uniformly sampled random edges, and that the size of this mass effect is unmeasured; a mass-matched control might shrink the gap. The experiments use three small open models and two synthetic tasks. Some induction examples fail the selected-versus-random comparison, and the extracted sketch does not recover the full known circuit.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested induction conditions. IOI results are not rows because they concern a different task. Section 3.5's extraction-knob sensitivities are summarized in method_sensitivity; the text gives no per-setting numerical gaps, and these are not direct tests of induction-head formation.

untested.parts: Composition with a previous-token head and the [A][B]…[A]→[B] mechanism are not tested. Overlap with known heads is described only qualitatively, in Section 3.3 and Figure 4.
Presence of heads with induction behaviour across GPT-2 Small, GPT-2 Medium and Pythia-410M is not measured. Only route-ablation gaps are reported.
Not tested; there are no training dynamics.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V1/V4 labels are not supported. The study is a methods paper that uses induction as a known-circuit benchmark, so it is T4. Its rows compare the study's own method with a random control, and they measure neither induction-head mechanism nor presence. IOI results are correctly excluded. Section 3.3's statement that known previous-token and induction heads 'show up almost always' is qualitative and relies on prior head labels, so it is not recorded as a version test.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not directly test head-to-head composition with an earlier previous-token head, or establish that the identified routes implement the full [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism.
Only GPT-2 Small, GPT-2 Medium, and Pythia-410M are tested on induction; the study does not test multiple training runs, other architectures, or modalities.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Zero selected attention-edge weights and renormalize remaining weights; compare with ablation of ten random edge sets of the same size.

conditions.value: n=100 clean prompts; single-token words after filtering

rows.measure: Mean target-logit drop, ΔS, and paired gap ΔS−ΔR
rows.uncertainty: ΔS ±1.97 and ΔR ±0.18 (standard deviations across prompts); 95% bootstrap CI for gap [+3.95, +4.72]; one-sided Wilcoxon p<10−10
rows.note: The text reports 0/100 examples where selected-edge ablation did not exceed random-edge ablation.
rows.check: The row measures the study's own method against a random-edge control (gap +4.33 on GPT-2 Small). It does not measure induction-head behaviour, composition with a previous-token head, or presence of induction heads, so it bears on no version. The model is not a small attention-only transformer.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Medium
rows.operation_detail: Zero selected attention-edge weights and renormalize remaining weights; compare with ablation of ten random edge sets of the same size.

conditions.value: n=100 clean prompts; single-token words after filtering

rows.measure: Mean target-logit drop, ΔS, and paired gap ΔS−ΔR
rows.uncertainty: ΔS ±1.93 and ΔR ±0.06 (standard deviations across prompts); 95% bootstrap CI excludes zero; one-sided Wilcoxon p<10−10
rows.note: The text reports 19/100 examples where selected-edge ablation did not exceed random-edge ablation.
rows.check: This is the method's own validation on GPT-2 Medium (gap +1.51; 19/100 fails). A route-ablation gap on induction prompts does not show that heads with induction behaviour exist in this model, so it is not a V4 test.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Zero selected attention-edge weights and renormalize remaining weights; compare with ablation of ten random edge sets of the same size.

conditions.value: n=100 clean prompts; single-token words after filtering

rows.measure: Mean target-logit drop, ΔS, and paired gap ΔS−ΔR
rows.uncertainty: ΔS ±1.79 and ΔR ±0.11 (standard deviations across prompts); 95% bootstrap CI excludes zero; one-sided Wilcoxon p<10−10
rows.note: The text reports 11/100 examples where selected-edge ablation did not exceed random-edge ablation.
rows.check: This is the method's own validation on Pythia-410M (gap +2.25; 11/100 fails). The measure is target-logit drop under extracted-edge ablation, not induction-head presence or mechanism.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Induction-task prompts on GPT-2 Small, GPT-2 Medium, and Pythia-410M
reader_labels.reason: Selected route ablations lower the induction target logit more than same-size random-edge ablations in all three models (r1–r3); this supports causal relevance of some routes, not the specified head-composition mechanism.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The tested route-ablation results and interpretation
reader_labels.reason: The study reports individual failures on Medium and Pythia and notes that selected edges remove more attention mass than random edges, so part of the gap may be a mass effect; it does not isolate the claimed head-to-head composition (r1–r3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Induction-task tests on GPT-2 Small, GPT-2 Medium, and Pythia-410M
reader_labels.reason: All three tested checkpoints show a positive selected-versus-random ablation gap on induction prompts (r1–r3).
